title: One session, end to end — ZCode
example_input: A user sets a goal in the desktop app, works through several turns, closes the app, resumes in the terminal, and lets the Goal system drive the session to a verified finish.
note: Every module link pins the exact commit this teardown is based on — zai-org/ZCode @ 3c5b2276 (package version 3.16.2, pinned by commit; there is no v3.16.2 tag).

steps.title: A prompt arrives on any surface
steps.narrative: The user types a task in the desktop app — or the same shared UI in a browser, or the terminal TUI. All three surfaces are clients of the same host services and the same agent; the desktop is an Electron shell around the shared UI, and even the CLI distribution can serve the web surface (zcode --web). What the surface contributes is presentation and host features, not a different agent.
steps.representation:
surface (desktop | web | tui)
  -> shared UI (packages/ui)
  -> host services (packages/services)
  -> zcode-protocol v4 session command

modules.label: desktop, browser and terminal interfaces, one repo
one zcode command: TUI, --web, or Agent CLI args

steps.title: The prompt becomes a cancellable runtime command
steps.narrative: Host and agent speak the zcode-protocol (v4): session commands in, session events out. Inside the runtime, executeTurn enqueues the prompt as a cancellable PromptRuntimeCommand on the single runtime command queue — the same queue that will later carry steering, background results and goal continuations, which is why all of them share one ordering and one Stop button.
steps.representation:
executeTurn(input):
  enqueueCancellableRuntimeCommand({
    kind: PromptRuntimeCommand,
    input, abortSignal })
  -> drained by the turn loop in order

modules.label: executeTurn enqueues a cancellable prompt command
protocol v4 session command handlers

steps.title: The turn loop assembles the request
steps.narrative: runRegularTurnLoop iterates without a cap. Each iteration drains queued commands, runs microcompact and auto-compact (a third consecutive rapid refill throws instead of spinning), initializes MCP and refreshes MCP tools if their list changed, then assembles the request: system sections, mode/todo/goal reminders, prefetched memory recall — and runs one model step.
steps.representation:
while (true):
  drain runtime commands
  microcompact(); autoCompactIfNeeded()
  initializeMcp(); refreshMcpToolsIfChanged()
  request = sections + reminders + recall
  step = model(request, tools)

modules.label: runRegularTurnLoop — the unbounded loop
MCP initialized and refreshed inside the loop
MAX_CONSECUTIVE_RAPID_REFILLS = 3 — the circuit breaker

steps.title: One model step, GLM by default
steps.narrative: The model step goes through the provider layer. The bundled built-in config (revision 33) puts the Z.ai Coding Plan template first — GLM-5.3 over the anthropic-messages API shape — ahead of 20 other templates over three API shapes. On the official coding-plan path, the gateway rewrites the public endpoints to the plan gateway paths.
steps.representation:
builtin config rev 33, template #1:
  zai-api: anthropic-messages
  baseUrl https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic
  models  GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash
  (gateway: /api/anthropic -> /api/v1/ultra-zai/...)

modules.label: zai-api — the first built-in template
the coding-plan gateway rewrite table

steps.title: Tool calls run through the permission service
steps.narrative: The model answers with tool calls. Each call is evaluated by the permission service from the tool's own capability metadata — risk level, side-effect scope, read-only/destructive — against the session's collaboration mode (plan, build, edit, yolo, guarded, auto), the rulesets and plan-mode policy. Hooks observe the decision as a PermissionRequest event. Approved calls execute; results return to the loop for the next iteration.
steps.representation:
toolCall -> PermissionService.evaluate(
  capability {risk, sideEffectScope, readOnly},
  mode in {plan|build|edit|yolo|guarded|auto},
  rulesets, planModePolicy)
  -> allow | ask | deny -> execute -> result

modules.label: the six collaboration modes
the PermissionService class
a tool's own permission spec (GoalRead shown)

steps.title: The turn is persisted as session events
steps.narrative: Everything the turn produced — messages, events, todos, usage — is written to the SQLite session store shared by all surfaces. This is what makes the surface disposable: close the desktop app here and the session, including its goal row (readTarget is a store read), can be resumed from the terminal with counters and state intact.
steps.representation:
SQLite session DB (node:sqlite):
  sessions / messages / events
  todos
  target row  <- the goal lives here
  (status, tokenBudget, tokensUsed, ...)

modules.label: readTarget — the goal as a store row
resume reads the goal back and injects its state

steps.title: Idle with an active goal: verifier first, then continuation
steps.narrative: The user had set a goal earlier (/goal, or the UI equivalent). Now the session goes idle with the goal still active, so continueActiveTargetIfIdle enqueues a target-continuation command. Executing it first runs the completion verifier — a separate, tool-less, JSON-only model request. Only if the verifier fails with a concrete next action does a continuation turn run, carrying the budget accounting and the audit checklist. The model never marks its own goal complete.
steps.representation:
continueActiveTargetIfIdle():
  enqueue(target-continuation, priority=next)
executeTargetContinuationCommand():
  if background tasks running -> defer
  verdict = verify(goal)   # no tools, JSON only
  if verdict.passed -> stop
  if no nextAction -> stop
  re-read goal; if changed -> stop
  turn(formatGoalContinuationPrompt(goal, verdict))

modules.label: continueActiveTargetIfIdle enqueues the continuation
executeTargetContinuationCommand — defer, verify, re-read
the continuation prompt: budget + completion audit
the verifier prompt: no tools, JSON only

steps.title: The same session, resumed anywhere — and stopped by accounting
steps.narrative: The cycle of work, idle, verify and continue repeats across surfaces — the goal was set in the desktop app and can be inspected in the TUI with /goal, paused, resumed or cleared by the user at any time. It ends in exactly three ways: the verifier passes (status complete), the token budget is exhausted (budget_limited), or the user stops it. Termination never depends on the working model deciding it is done.
steps.representation:
goal status transitions:
  active -> complete        (verifier passed)
  active -> budget_limited  (tokensUsed >= tokenBudget)
  active <-> paused         (user: /goal pause|resume)
  any    -> (cleared)       (user: /goal clear)

modules.label: the /goal handler: set, pause, resume, clear
the four goal statuses
